title: Home guide: friction on different surfaces
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Forces, magnets and light (Mighty Metals and Why Do Cat's Eyes Glow at Night?)
source: Written for science/y3 lesson 9 (Home practical guide and safety card: friction surfaces (portal worksheet))
intro: Read it all first, then do it with an adult nearby.

practical.aim: Find out which surface has the most friction.
equipment: A toy car or a small box
A towel, a tray and a clear floor space
safety: Keep the floor clear so nobody trips
An adult knows what you are doing and stays nearby
Clear a space; tidy up and wash your hands afterwards
method: Put the car on the floor and give it a gentle push.
Do the same on the tray and on the towel, pushing just as hard.
Put the surfaces in order, most friction first (the car goes the shortest distance).
